julia-cs: Hey team, enterprise customer (AcmeCorp) reporting intermittent requests routing to EU instead of US. They say this started after upgrading our SDK, ~last 24h. High P50 latency for them. Can someone take a look? :confused:
sara-support: Thanks Julia — can you paste an example request (headers + any query params) they send? Also which SDK version?
julia-cs: SDK v2.1.0. Here is their repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" \
  -H "Client-Region: us-west" \
  -H "client-region: EU-WEST" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
They say sometimes they see responses from eu-1 (wrong) even though they set us-west.
sara-support: whoa two region headers with different casing/values. hmm. can you attach a router trace or request id?
julia-cs: example request-id: req_0a9f3b. They attached edge logs (pasted below).
```
EDGE_LOG: recv headers: Host: api.redwood.ai; Client-Region: us-west; client-region: EU-WEST; X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.12
ROUTER_DECIDE: selected_edge: eu-1 ; reason: header_priority(first_header)
ROUTER_DEBUG: header_keys_order: [client-region, Client-Region, x-client-region]
```
alejandro-sre: That log is telling — our router code does header lookup by iterating request.headers (in insertion order) and picks the first matching header key "client-region" (case-sensitive lookup). If upstream proxies reorder headers or the client sends mixed-case duplicates, the selected value can flip. This is a class bug: we don't normalize header names before decision.
sara-support: Is this why fallback happened to EU? The first header seen was the lowercase one ("client-region: EU-WEST").
alejandro-sre: Exactly. A few notes:
- Some client proxies (or the customer's HTTP client) preserve original-case header when adding, or add the header later.
- Our edge (Fastly/Cloudfront) may coalesce headers unpredictably and the router reads them in an order we don't control.
- Router decision should normalize to lowercase and prefer a canonical header name (e.g., x-client-region) and we should define precedence with query param and token claims.
sara-support: Can we reproduce locally? Any quick repro steps?
alejandro-sre: Yes, minimal repro: run a netcat server and send two headers in different order:
```
echo -e "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.ai\r\nclient-region: EU-WEST\r\nClient-Region: us-west\r\n\r\n" | nc localhost 8080
```
Then inspect router decision log. If insertion order returns `client-region` first we'll pick EU.
julia-cs: Customer confirms they were using a proxy that normalizes headers to lower-case first for some requests.
sara-support: Short-term workaround for them? Can we suggest sending query param region=us-west or use x-client-region header?
alejandro-sre: Workaround options:
- Use query param `?region=us-west` (we treat query param as higher precedence than headers currently)
- Send a single canonical header `x-client-region: us-west` (no duplicates)
- Upgrade to SDK patch I'll propose that always sets `x-client-region` and removes any legacy `client-region` header.
sara-support: OK I'll pass those to AcmeCorp. Can we hotfix router to normalize? Severity is high for multi-tenant customers.
alejandro-sre: Proposed fix (short-term): in edge adapter (node layer right before routing) run:
```
// pseudo
const norm = {};
for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(req.headers)) {
  norm[k.toLowerCase()] = norm[k.toLowerCase()] || v;
}
req.normalizedHeaders = norm;
// then router uses req.normalizedHeaders['x-client-region'] || req.normalizedHeaders['client-region']
```
We can ship this as a config toggle and enable for affected POPs.
tim-engineer: I'll take the code change, add tests for duplicate/mixed-case headers, and coordinate a canary. ETA: 3h for PR, 6h for canary + monitor.
sara-support: assign to Tim and pls link the PR here when ready. I'll send the workaround to the customer and offer to monitor.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: canary/edge-normalize-headers -> 10% POPs at 2950004500 UTC, rollback window 30m. :rocket:
router-bot: Routing-rule audit: adding explicit precedence doc for region sources (token claim > query param > x-client-region header > legacy client-region header > ip-geo fallback).
julia-cs: Thanks team. I'll tell the customer the workaround and confirm after the canary. :thumbsup:
sara-support: filing followup: ACTIONS: tim-engineer PR + tests, enable toggle in eu/us POP canary, update SDK to set x-client-region, notify CS.
alejandro-sre: Also adding a small telemetry metric: count of requests with duplicate region headers and mismatched values (we saw ~120 in last 6h from AcmeCorp).
sara-support: great, closing loop once canary is green.
